steps.title: Open the live network map
steps.say: Ports, plants and warehouses, with a sample of the inbound shipments at sea right now. Every dot is a purchase order on its way to a plant.

steps.title: Inject a 21-day port capacity reduction
steps.say: Shanghai loses 70% of its capacity for three weeks. A queue model turns that into a delay for each shipment, depending on the day it reaches the port.

steps.title: Affected shipments and finished products
steps.say: Which orders are delayed, which components they carry, and which finished products contain those components once the bill of materials is followed all the way down.

steps.title: Forecast inventory depletion by facility
steps.say: Each plant is simulated day by day for 12 weeks: stock on hand, delayed receipts, daily use. The chart shows days of cover for the components that run out first. Then one shipment's arrival forecast and its supplier's risk.

steps.title: Run 1,000 Monte Carlo futures
steps.say: The cut may be deeper or longer than assumed, and every shipment's transit time is noisy. A background job simulates a thousand futures, and the same thousand without the disruption for comparison.

steps.title: Optimize the recovery
steps.say: A mixed-integer model chooses which delayed shipments to fly, what to buy from a second source that does not use the port, and what to pull from warehouse reserve.

steps.title: Compare baseline and recovery plan
steps.say: Three plans judged by the same daily simulator, not by the optimizer's own arithmetic: do nothing, fly the most delayed shipments, and the optimized plan.
